hook: Cosoreanu spent nearly two decades rising through GE's energy technology divisions, engineering, program management, and eventually product and CTO roles in grid automation, before taking the CTO seat at GE Vernova as the company builds the grid infrastructure and automation technology the energy transition depends on.
name: Claudia Cosoreanu

quote.text: Innovation without customer focus means that engineers get to have fun, but it does not mean that they are solving real problems. Co-creation and collaboration with the end customer is as important as being creative.

moniker: Chief Technology Officer at GE Vernova

reading.body:
Claudia Cosoreanu holds the CTO seat at GE Vernova, making her the person responsible for the technology direction of one of the companies building the grid infrastructure that AI scaling depends on.

Her path to that role followed a single consistent thread. She joined GE in digital energy in 2002, spent roughly a decade in engineering and program management, moved into innovation strategy at GE Research, and then held the Grid Automation CTO position before being named company-wide CTO in 2025. Each step stayed inside grid protection, automation, and energy systems. That depth matters because grid automation, not generation alone, is what allows variable renewable sources to be integrated reliably, and reliable integration is what determines whether new power capacity actually reaches the data centers that need it.

The data covers her career progression and stated philosophy but does not include specifics about GE Vernova's technology roadmap, any particular products she has led to market, or how her work connects to AI infrastructure demand in any direct or quantified way. Her Stanford machine learning certificate is noted in the record but without context about how or whether it shapes her technical priorities. What the record does establish clearly is that the person now setting technology direction for a major grid automation company built her expertise from inside that domain over nearly twenty years, rather than arriving from adjacent fields.
